ICC printer profiling · free & open source

Make your printer print the colour you actually chose.

ChromIQ builds a custom ICC profile for your exact printer, ink and paper — the colour fingerprint that makes prints match your screen. It drives ArgyllCMS through a calm five-step wizard, so you never touch the command line.

Download for macOS, Windows & Linux View on GitHub

Free under the GPLv3. Needs ArgyllCMS 3.5.0 — ChromIQ finds it for you on first launch.

The five steps

From a blank sheet to an accurate profile — in order.

Each step has a Guided path with sensible defaults and a Manual path that exposes every ArgyllCMS control, side by side. A clickable ⓘ on every screen explains what to do.

01

Create Chart

Generate a test chart of colour patches, sized to your paper and instrument. Guided picks sensible settings from an empirical patch-capacity database; Manual exposes every targen / printtarg flag with a live preview of the exact sheet.

02

Print Chart

Print it the way profiling needs — with colour management off. A PostScript pipeline on macOS, an automatic TIFF fallback for AirPrint / driverless printers, or the native OS dialog with the driver's colour controls locked. Preflight checks paper size and orientation first.

03

Measure

Read the printed patches with your spectrophotometer. Keyboard-driven strip reading — Enter confirms, F/B step forward and back — plus read-again-and-average to cut instrument noise. ChromIQ knows your instrument's reading pace, checks every strip's speed live and tells you when a swipe was too fast to be reliable — with optional sounds for every event, so your eyes can stay on the chart.

04

Build Profile

Turn the measurements into an ICC profile with colprof. RGB, CMYK and multi-channel DeviceN targets; CIECAM02 viewing-condition presets; media attributes embedded in the profile header.

05

Check & Refine

See the profile's accuracy in ΔE, inspect the 3D gamut volume it can reproduce, and run a second-pass pre-conditioning refinement that samples harder where your printer is least accurate.

New in the latest release

Profile your scanner — or your camera — too.

Reuse a chart you already measured, or load a target you own — a Wolf Faust IT8, an X-Rite ColorChecker, a LaserSoft chart. ChromIQ lays a reading grid over your scan (or photo) so it sits exactly on the patches, then builds a scanner or camera ICC profile.

  • Reads bought targets straight from ArgyllCMS — with corrected recognition files bundled for the ones Argyll got wrong.
  • Converts the target’s reference data for you (X-Rite .cxf, spectral .txt) — no command line.
  • Average several scans to cut noise; pick a Matrix or LUT profile.

More than the wizard

Serious colour science, with the sharp edges filed off.

Guided & Manual

Sensible one-click defaults, or every ArgyllCMS flag exposed with a live preview — same window, your choice.

Prints without colour management

A raw PostScript/TIFF path that bypasses ColorSync and driver colour correction, so the chart prints exactly as sent.

3D gamut viewer

Rotate the colour volume your profile reproduces and compare it against a reference space like Adobe RGB.

Scanner & camera profiling

Reuse a measured chart — or a bought IT8 / ColorChecker target — to build an input profile for a scanner or a camera.

Calibration, then profile

Optional linearisation pass (printcal / applycal) before profiling, for printers without built-in calibration.

i1Profiler interoperability

Import and export i1Profiler charts and measurements, so ChromIQ fits into an existing X-Rite workflow.

Device-links & soft-proofing

Build device-link profiles and soft-proof an image with an out-of-gamut mask before you commit ink to paper.

Plain-language help everywhere

Every screen has a clickable ⓘ that explains the step, and what you need, in words a beginner can follow.

Every run keeps its own work

A profile run holds its own chart, measurement, settings and description, so going back to an older run shows what that run was actually made with. Nothing you made is deleted — only archived, with the date.

Verification runs, kept as history

Measure a chart printed through a finished profile and the result is filed by date with its own report. Earlier checks are never overwritten, so you can watch a profile drift over months.

Sounds during measurement

A strip accepted, a patch misread, a session finished — each can play a sound, so you can keep your eyes on the chart instead of the screen.

Twelve languages

German, Spanish, French, Italian, Dutch, Portuguese, Swedish, Norwegian, Polish, Russian, Japanese and Chinese — every button, message, tooltip and help text, not just the menus.

Companion app

ChromIQ Patches — the chart editor, on its own.

The test-chart / patch-set editor is also a small standalone app. Build and combine patch sets, generate colour distributions, and inspect them as a 3D point cloud — then hand the result to ChromIQ or to i1Profiler. Free and open source, like everything here.

  • Design and merge patch sets, with live counts.
  • RGB, CMYK — and CMYK plus extra ink channels (OGV and friends).
  • See the whole set as a rotatable 3D RGB cube.
  • Export straight to i1Profiler or ArgyllCMS.

Under the hood

What it runs on.

Instruments
i1Pro · i1Pro 2 · i1Pro 3 · i1Pro 3 Plus · ColorMunki (i1Studio / ColorChecker Studio) · SpectroScan — plus i1iSis charts via i1Profiler (ChromIQ makes the chart and imports the measurement; i1Profiler does the reading)
Colour engine
ArgyllCMS 3.5.0 — not bundled; ChromIQ finds it for you on first launch
ChromIQ's own engines
A chart layout engine that sizes patches by minimum width or by columns and rows, with instrument-safe margins and a live preview of the exact sheet · a strip-reading engine with sounds, live pace feedback and per-strip re-reads · five combinable patch-set generators · a verification target built from your profile's own gamut
Platforms
macOS · Windows · Linux (x86_64 & aarch64, beta)
Languages
13, including German, French, Spanish, Italian, Japanese, Chinese
Licence
GPLv3 — free and open source
